categories.main_business_segments: ON Semiconductor (onsemi) operates through three primary business segments: Power Solutions Group (PSG), Advanced Solutions Group (ASG), and Intelligent Sensing Group (ISG). PSG focuses on analog, discrete, module, and integrated semiconductor products for power applications. ASG develops analog, mixed-signal, power management ICs, and sensor interface devices, while ISG specializes in CMOS image sensors, image signal processors, and related sensing technologies.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages advanced semiconductor technologies including silicon carbide (SiC), wide band gap (WBG) MOSFETs, IGBT, CMOS image sensors, and integrated power modules. Manufacturing is conducted through a global network of front-end wafer fabs and back-end assembly/test facilities, with a mix of internal production and third-party contractors. ON has invested in expanding SiC manufacturing capacity and employs platform-based design and integration for rapid product development.
categories.primary_customers_markets: onsemi serves a broad customer base, with a primary focus on the automotive and industrial sectors, which together accounted for 80% of 2023 revenue. Key applications include electric vehicles (EV/HEV), ADAS, industrial automation, energy infrastructure, and factory automation. Customers include OEMs, contract manufacturers, and distributors, with long-term supply agreements in place for strategic end-customers.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates globally, with significant sales in Asia (notably Hong Kong and Singapore), Europe (United Kingdom), and the United States. Manufacturing, R&D, and design centers are distributed across North America, Europe, and Asia, with major facilities in the U.S., Czech Republic, South Korea, Malaysia, Philippines, and Vietnam. In 2023, 26% of revenue was billed from Hong Kong, 24% from Singapore, 21% from the UK, and 19% from the U.S.
categories.supply_chain_position: onsemi is primarily a midstream and downstream supplier, designing, manufacturing, and assembling semiconductor components and solutions that are integrated into end products by OEMs and other customers. The company sources raw materials (e.g., silicon, SiC wafers) and utilizes both internal fabs and external foundries/assembly partners, positioning itself as a key supplier in the electronics value chain.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategy centers on profitable growth by targeting high-growth megatrends in automotive electrification, industrial automation, and intelligent sensing. R&D investments are focused on SiC power technologies, intelligent sensing for automotive safety and automation, and high-efficiency energy solutions. onsemi is optimizing its manufacturing footprint, pursuing operational efficiencies, and realigning resources to accelerate innovation in high-margin products and markets.
categories.revenue_model: onsemi generates revenue primarily through the sale of semiconductor products to both distributors (52% of 2023 revenue) and direct customers (48%). Additional revenue streams include product development agreements and manufacturing services, though these are minor compared to product sales. The company also enters into long-term supply agreements with certain customers, often including minimum purchase commitments.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include Infineon, STMicroelectronics, Texas Instruments, Wolfspeed, Nexperia, Analog Devices, Renesas, Monolithic Power Systems, NXP, Sony, Samsung, and Omnivision. onsemi differentiates itself through its focus on intelligent power and sensing, SiC leadership, and integration capabilities, holding strong positions in automotive and industrial markets. The company faces competition from both broad-line semiconductor firms and specialized niche players.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2023, onsemi reported $8.25 billion in revenue, a slight decrease of 0.9% from 2022, with net income of $2.18 billion and operating income of $2.54 billion. The company maintains strong gross margins (47.1% in 2023) and has demonstrated robust profitability. While revenue was flat in 2023 due to industry headwinds, the company has a history of growth, particularly in automotive and SiC-based products, and continues to invest in capacity expansion.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: onsemi’s value proposition lies in its ability to deliver intelligent power and sensing solutions that enable higher efficiency, reduced system cost, and enhanced performance for automotive and industrial applications. The company emphasizes its leadership in SiC and WBG technologies, integration of sensing and power, and ability to support customers with global manufacturing and logistics. Differentiation is driven by innovation, quality, and deep application expertise in high-growth markets.
